department_distribution.key_insight: Engineering and Data & AI constitute 49.5% of total enterprise headcount.

gender_distribution.key_insight: Female representation stands at 40.5%, demonstrating strong gender diversity balance across technical and business functions.

experience_analysis.key_insight: The workforce has an average experience of 7.5 years, with a healthy distribution from entry-level apprentices to veteran technical leads.

salary_analysis.key_insight: Engineering commands the highest median compensation ($135,300), reflecting high market premiums for deep engineering and AI specialization.

top_technical_skills.key_insight: AWS (129 practitioners) and SQL (116 practitioners) form the organizational foundational technology stack.

department_performance.key_insight: Product leads company performance with an average appraisal score of 3.73 / 5.0.

skill_gap_analysis.key_insight: Sales & Marketing displays lower average technical skill inventory (4.4 skills/person), highlighting prime candidates for targeted cross-functional upskilling.

exp_vs_perf.key_insight: Correlation between experience and performance rating is 0.04, demonstrating that high performance occurs across both newer agile talent and tenured leaders.

training_impact.key_insight: Employees who completed corporate certifications achieve a +0.01 higher average performance appraisal score compared to untrained peers.

correlation_findings.key_insight: Job Satisfaction (-0.06) and Work-Life Balance (-0.07) show strong negative correlations with Attrition, signaling retention sensitivity to workplace well-being.
